 J U D G M E N T

The present claim petition is filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .10,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 24.09.2023 at about 10.30 a.m., when he was walking in front of Poultry Farm belonged to one Mr.Girish on Doddabelavangala - Sasalu Road, a Maruthi Eco Van bearing Regn.No.KA-41-ME-4582, driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to him.

Due to the accident, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and thereafter, he was shifted to Manipal Hospital, Bashetty Halli, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent a sum of .3,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was doing Agricultural Work and also having cows and doing milk business and earning a sum of .15,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of Maruthi van by its driver.
The respondents, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In spite of service of notice, respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal and hence, he has been placed ex-parte.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal and filed the written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.2 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.2 also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondent No.2 contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Respondent No.2 admitted the aspect of issue of Bundle Motor Policy (3 years TP + 1 years OD) bearing No.3311/01038335/000/00 in favour of 1st respondent in respect of Maruthi Eco New Car valid from 04.07.2023 to 03.07.2026 and contended that the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
Further contended that the first respondent had been willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
Further contended that the petitioner was the main architect for causing the alleged accident as he negligently tried to cross the road without observing the movement of the vehicle on main road.
The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:

sentences.text:
1. Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 24.09.2023 at about 11.30 p.m., while petitioner being a pedestrian on Doddabelavangala to Sasalu Road Near Poultry Farm of Mr.Girish, Sonnenahalli,
Doddaballapura Taluk, due to the rash and negligent driving of Maruthi Eco Van bearing Regn.No.KA-41-ME-4582 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order or award?

6. In order to prove the contentions of the petition, the petitioner got examined as PW.1, son of petitioner by name Sri.Shivakumara.G got examined as PW.2 and one witness by name Sri.Kiran Kumar.S.M. got examined as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and closed their side of evidence.
The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary.

7. Heard argument of the side and perused the materials placed on record.
8.

Findings of this tribunal on the above issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative;
Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:-
-:REASONS:-
9. Issue No.1:- The petitioner contended that on 24.09.2023 at about 10.30 a.m., accident occurred while petitioner was walking on Doddabelavangala to Sasalu Road, Near Poultry Farm of Mr.Girish,
Sonnenahalli, Doddaballapura Taluk, due to rash and negligent driving of Maruthi Eco Van bearing Regn.No.KA-41-ME-4582 by its driver in which he sustained grievous injuries.
10.
In order to prove rash and negligent driving of Maruthi Eco Van bearing Regn.No.KA-41-ME- 4582 by its driver, the petitioner himself got examined as PW.1.
In the chief examination, PW.1 deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of Maruthi van by its driver, the accident occurred.

On perusal of cross-examination of PW.1, nothing has been elicited from PW.1 to disprove or disbelieve the case of petitioner. Nothing to dispute or rebut the contention of petitioner related to the accident and cause of accident could be elicited during the cross examination.
11. Further, in order to prove the accident and negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, the petitioner produced Ex.P.2, first information statement.
Ex . P.2
discloses that relative of petitioner by name Sri.Kiran Kumar.S.M has lodged the complaint with the police on 24.09.2023.

On the basis of first information lodged by relative of petitioner, the police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the Gangadharaiah Alias Gangadharappa vs Dolaram T on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64340724/
3 offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC.

sentences.text: In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of Maruthi van by its driver.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The petitioner also furnished spot mahazar which is marked as Ex.P.3.
The said document discloses that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said document.
In mahazar, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that the facts, as stated in the mahazar, are contrary to the actual facts at the place of accident.
Ex.P.4 is the Wound certificate which discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner in the road traffic accident.
In the said document also, it is mentioned about sustaining of injuries by petitioner due to road traffic accident.
The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC, which is marked as Ex.P.5.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
12. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of record, it discloses that the accident was caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in which petitioner sustained injuries.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.5, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Maruthi Eco Van bearing Regn.No.KA-41-ME- 4582 by its driver and same has resulted in injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance.
14. The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained fracture to his legs, left hand, right eyebrows and bleeding all over the body.

In order to prove the injuries, petitioner has produced Ex.P.4 - wound certificate issued by Manipal Hospital, wherein the doctor diagnosed that petitioner sustained degloving injury over left leg, laceration over right thumb measuring 5cm x 1cm and multiple abrasions over the face, right knee, right forearm and right lower limbs and doctor has Gangadharaiah Alias Gangadharappa vs Dolaram T on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64340724/
4 opined that injuries are simple in nature.

sentences.text: The petitioner has not produced discharge summary to show that he has taken treatment at the hospital.
In order to prove the disability, the petitioner neither produced disability certificate nor examined the doctor.
The petitioner not furnished satisfactory materials in order to ascertain and adjudicate the aspect of disability, as contended by him.
The petitioner has produced medical bills which are marked as Ex.P.6, totally amounting to .8,352/-.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut the medical bills furnished by petitioner.
No satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal in order to controvert or rebut the bills furnished by petitioner.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to prove the aspect of disability.
The petitioner not furnished satisfactory materials and also not examined any witness in order to prove the aspect of disability caused to him due to accidental injuries.
The petitioner also not furnished satisfactory materials to substantiate his contention regarding occupation and income.
No satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal to assess and ascertain the loss of income to the petitioner due to accidental injuries.
The petitioner not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to assess and ascertain the disability caused to his and to assess the loss of income caused to him due to the disability.

The materials placed before the Tribunal are not sufficient and satisfactory to assess and ascertain the disability caused to the petitioner due to accident and to assess the loss of income due to the disability.
No satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal to show that accidental injuries deprived the earning capacity of petitioner and caused impact on his income as well as earning capacity.
So, in the absence of proper evidence, this tribunal cannot award compensation under the head of future loss of income and other heads.

By considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also the injuries sustained by the petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of .50,000/-
(including medical bills).
15.

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs.
Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

sentences.text: 16. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Maruthi Eco Van bearing Regn.No.KA-41-ME-4582 by its driver.
So, the respondents, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 is answered Partly in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.

sentences.text: Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
Entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of petitioner as amount is meager one.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
The Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
